evidence_summary: Venue: International Journal of Advanced Technology and Engineering Exploration, Vol 13(138), May 2026, pp. 731-748, open access CC BY, research article, Scopus-indexed record, received 26-Oct-2025 and accepted 18-May-2026. Evaluation type: physical cloud testbed (an AWS EKS cluster with one control plane node and two bare-metal workers, c5d.metal and c5n.metal, ap-south-1 Mumbai region, described by the authors as a production-level EKS cluster used as a proof of concept). Baseline: Kubernetes Default Scheduler (KDS) with default plugins. Headline numbers with locators: factorial-500 workload total cluster CE 2523.65 gCO2eq for CAKS vs 2530.64 gCO2eq for KDS, a 6.99 gCO2eq or 0.70% saving (pp. 740-741, Figure 6). Factorial 40,000: 3278.68 vs 3279.78 gCO2eq, about 0.003% per the text on p. 741 (Figure 8 prints 0.03). Factorial 60,000: 3991.71 vs 4057.52 gCO2eq, 65.81 gCO2eq or 1.62% (p. 741, Figure 10). Ten-day study mean improvements 1.33%, 0.27%, 2.06% for the three job sets with one-sample t-tests, all 95% CIs above zero (Table 3, p. 743). Conclusion states reduction of up to 2.06% vs KDS (p. 746).
ai_rationale: The artifact is a CarbonScore scoring plugin inside the Kubernetes scheduling framework plus a DaemonSet carbon collector that reads node power from MSR via Turbostat and carbon intensity from the ElectricityMap API, and pods are placed on the lowest-emission node. Q1 yes (the plugin independently produces placement decisions), Q2 yes (decisions act directly on containerized pods in a Kubernetes cluster), Q3 yes (explicit cluster-level carbon emission minimization with measured gCO2eq outcomes). Title shows container platform, scheduling decision, and carbon relation, so the strict core boundary is met. Real-hardware evaluation rather than simulation. Caveats for the reviewer: the journal is a low-profile open-access venue, the cluster has only two worker nodes in a single region, and the reductions are small (0.27% to 2.06% means). These affect weight in synthesis, not eligibility.

Table 2 (p. 72): on 2X-Server-2021 PAX 237 ms P99 at 345 W vs HPA 1171 ms at 371 W and Cilantro 3169 ms at 334 W, on 4X-Server-2014 PAX 680 ms at 199 W vs HPA 1305 ms at 274 W, on the mixed cluster PAX 193 ms at 238 W vs HPA 994 ms at 321 W. Q1: PAX independently produces control decisions, Bayesian optimization (Meta AX platform) jointly selects pod replica counts and pod-to-node placement and applies them through the Kubernetes API (patch_namespaced_deployment), bypassing the default scheduler. Q2: the decisions act directly on containerized workloads (Kubernetes pod scaling and placement across heterogeneous nodes). Q3: an identifiable sustainability outcome is present, per-configuration CPU package power is measured with Kepler and reported (PAX reaches the lowest power on the 4X-Server-2014 and mixed clusters), and the embodied carbon of old vs new servers is quantified with ACT to support the carbon argument for hardware reuse. Caveats for synthesis: the BO objective in the reported experiments is P99 latency only, carbon and energy appear as measured outcomes and motivation rather than as an optimization signal, the authors call the results preliminary, and only one benchmark was used. It is nevertheless English primary research with evaluable testbed evidence against named baselines, so it belongs in the core intervention synthesis, flagged as a workshop paper per the survey's locked rule.
